cohort: The study included 198 infants born extremely premature who underwent routine cerebral magnetic resonance imaging (cMRI) at term-equivalent age.
finding: 47% of extremely preterm infants showed cerebral abnormalities on routine cMRI at term-equivalent age, with significant risk factors including lower Apgar scores, lower umbilical artery and first neonatal pH, asphyxia, late-onset sepsis, and prolonged respiratory support/supplemental oxygen.
